findings.title: m:scr and m:sty are ignored, so a different symbol becomes a plain letter
findings.scenario: Doc: run x∈ then <m:r><m:rPr><m:scr m:val="double-struck"/><m:sty m:val="p"/></m:rPr><m:t>R</m:t></m:r>. A person reads x ∈ ℝ; output is \(x∈R\). Script: ℒ = L + M gives \(L=L+M\). Fraktur: 𝔤 ⊂ g gives \(g⊂g\). Bold: <m:sty m:val="b"/> on x, then =(x,y): bold x = (x, y) gives \(x=(x,y)\). Bold-italic A next to italic A gives \(AA\). Two distinct symbols collapse into one, and no note is written.
findings.evidence: Ran rounds 1 and 2, cases S1-S8 and R1-R4, through parseSourceArtifact. KaTeX parsed every result and parser_messages was empty. Read: runToLatex only asks about m:nor. The XSD allows scr and sty in CT_RPR. From memory, not run: pandoc writes \mathbb and \mathbf in this shape.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this. It reproduces exactly, on the frozen tree, through both parseSourceArtifact and the real publish path.

REPRODUCTION (note block text, with has_parser_messages=false for the whole document):
- double-struck R after x∈ gives \(x∈R\)
- script L then =L+M gives \(L=L+M\)
- fraktur g then ⊂g gives \(g⊂g\)
- sty=b x then =(x,y) gives \(x=(x,y)\)
- sty=bi A then italic A gives \(AA\)

KaTeX parses each one, and in its MathML output the two letters come out as identical mi elements with no mathvariant. For S1 to S7, I also built the same formula with the properties removed, and the output was byte-identical. So the properties have no effect at all.

Why nothing catches it: runToLatex (line 161) reads only m:nor. keepsEveryCharacter passes because the ASCII letter survives, so refuse() never fires and no note or banner appears.

REACHABILITY: this is the format's standard storage, not an invented shape.
- The ISO/IEC 29500 text on Microsoft Learn says m:scr stores the character "between U+0000 and U+007F" along with the script, and the application maps it to the Unicode range. Its own example is m:scr fraktur or double-struck plus m:sty p on the letter a. The m:sty entry says the same, with values b, i, bi and p.
- The texmath OMML writer source, which pandoc uses, has TextDoubleStruck -> [scr "double-struck", sty "p"], the same for script and fraktur, TextBold -> [sty "b"] and TextBoldItalic -> [sty "bi"]. The claim's "from memory" pandoc evidence is now backed by source I read, though not by a run.
- The texmath reader also maps these properties to distinct text types, so another consumer treats them as meaningful.

NOT VERIFIED: I did not observe Word itself writing this. Word and pandoc are not installed here, and I did not download them. No real Word file with m:scr was available. The repo samples have no app.xml and were built by hand, and the f3-gold README confirms there is no MS Word. Reachability rests on the normative text and the texmath source.

CONTRACT: the f3-gold README requires "语义正确或走诚实降级,没有第三种", and the code comment says a wrong formula is never guessed at. This output is that third kind. The project's own baseline-second-corpus-F3.txt already marks 双线体, 花体, 粗体大写 and 期望双线 as WRONG, so this is a known red in the second corpus, not a new discovery. I read that file but did not re-run its checker, because the checker writes under D:.

SCOPE NOTES FOR THE FIX:
1. There is a second path. ommlLines (lines 299-300) also reads only m:nor. A run with m:sty b plus m:brk or w:br goes around runToLatex and gives \(a=\) \(x+x\). A fix only at line 161 would miss it.
2. Do not refuse on m:sty p alone. In my run a function name carrying sty=p correctly gives \sin{x} with no collapse. As I recall, Word writes this on function names, but I did not confirm that here. Refusing would degrade good formulas.
3. Severity depends on the document. A lone x∈R is still guessable, and the second corpus's gold accepts a lone bold x as plain x. The real damage is when a styled letter collapses into a plain letter already in the same formula, such as ℒ vs L or bold x vs x. Those cases stand as major.

Controls: Unicode ℝ and 𝐱 stored directly are preserved (\(x∈ℝ\), \(𝐱=x\)), which shows the loss comes only from the property path.

Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.math.script , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.math.style , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgm/texmath/master/src/Text/TeXMath/Writers/OMML.hs , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgm/texmath/master/src/Text/TeXMath/Readers/OMML.hs

findings.title: A structure tracked-deleted through m:ctrlPr/w:del stays in the formula
findings.scenario: Doc: y= then <m:nary><m:naryPr><m:chr m:val="∑"/><m:ctrlPr><w:del .../></m:ctrlPr></m:naryPr><m:sub><w:del>i=1</w:del></m:sub><m:sup><w:del>n</w:del></m:sup><m:e><w:del>x</w:del></m:e></m:nary><w:ins>x</w:ins>. A person reads y = x; output is \(y=\sum{}x\), a sum nobody kept. Deleted fraction after C: \(C\frac{}{}\). Deleted radical: \(\sqrt{}x\). Deleted integral: \(y=\int{}x\). Deleted parens with inner text re-inserted: \(\left(\right)a+bc\). Deleted parens with contents kept (a+b)c, final a+bc: \(\left(a+b\right)c\). Deleted hat: \(\hat{x}\). Deleted fraction with contents kept: \(\frac{a}{b}\) for ab. The inserted-then-deleted form <w:ins><w:del/></w:ins> in ctrlPr gives the same result.
findings.evidence: Ran T1, T4-T7, T9-T11 (round 1), R8-R12, R14 (round 2), X3, X4 (round 3). All parsed in KaTeX and none was declared. Read: every *Pr element is skipped at line 186, so the mark is never seen. Read in the XSD: wml.xsd EG_RPrMath puts w:ins and w:del directly in CT_CtrlPr, so this is a legal position. Not confirmed in Word: the exact shape Word writes, especially the contents-kept variants. T2 and T3 (ctrlPr/w:rPr/w:del, ctrlPr/w:moveFrom) give the same output but are outside that XSD.

verdict.reasoning:
**Verdict: I could not refute the core defect.** A structure that is tracked-deleted through `m:ctrlPr/w:del`, with its contents in `w:del`, stays in the formula with no notice. Three parts of the claim are narrower than stated (see "Where the claim is narrower").

**Reproduced through `parseSourceArtifact`, with real .docx files**

All outputs parse in KaTeX and all have declared=false.

| Case | Final text a person reads | Output | KaTeX draws |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sum, empty mark and mark holding rPr | y=x | `\(y=\sum{}x\)` | ∑ |
| Integral | y=x | `\(y=\int{}x\)` | ∫ |
| Radical | x | `\(\sqrt{}x\)` | surd SVG emitted |
| Parens, inner text re-inserted | a+bc | `\(\left(\right)a+bc\)` | () |
| Fraction after C, also the ins>del form | C | `\(C\frac{}{}\)` | no glyph, frac-line present |

Controls behave correctly:
- A structure wrapped whole in `w:del` gives `\(C\)`.
- A live fraction stays.
- A fraction marked `ctrlPr/w:ins` stays.
- A whole `m:oMath` inside `w:del` disappears.

Cause: line 186 skips every `*Pr` element, so the mark is never read. `keepsEveryCharacter` cannot catch it, because no source character is lost.

**Refutation attempts that failed**
1. **"No real producer writes this."**
   - ECMA-376 defines `del (Deleted Math Control Character)` as a child of `ctrlPr`, and its example is a deleted fraction bar.
   - MS-OI29500 has a Word-specific note on this exact element about its rPr child, and that note does not say Word ignores it.
   - Two third-party sources say Word tracks structures this way. Morrison-Lab #3422 reports "3 m:ctrlPr carrying w:ins, 6 carrying w:del" in a hand-edited document. manuscript-markdown PR #735 says Word puts the wrapper on runs and the structure's mark in its own ctrlPr.
2. **"A later step cleans it up."** A grep of `server/src/services` and `client/src` found nothing that strips empty shells. This was a grep only; I did not run materialization.
3. **"The project accepts this."** It does not. The F3 gold README allows only a semantically correct result or an honest degrade. The project's own `baseline-second-corpus-F3.txt` already marks this shape WRONG under the label 结构删除真形状, so the finding is not new.

**Limit on the evidence:** I did not observe Word's output. Word is not installed here, and the F3 docx with this mark is generated (no `docProps/app.xml`). The third-party sources are also weak:
- #3422 was filed by an AI agent and has no sample file.
- PR #735's description says "Not checked in Word itself", while a later commit says it was verified against Accept All and Reject All.

Reachability is therefore a well-supported inference, not a demonstration.

**Where the claim is narrower**
- **It is an incomplete fix, not a regression.** The pre-patch module gave `y=\sum_{i=1}^{n}{x}x`, `C\frac{1}{i}`, `\sqrt{2}x` and `\left(a+b\right)a+bc`, which also kept the deleted contents. The change shrank the error.
- **The deleted fraction is the weak example.** `\frac{}{}` emits no glyph, and its frac-line has nothing to span, so it probably looks right on screen. That is inferred from the HTML, since no browser was used; the raw text still carries the shell. The clearly visible cases are ∑, ∫, () and, going by the emitted SVG, the surd.
- **The contents-kept variants are unestablished.** `\(\left(a+b\right)c\)`, `\(\hat{x}\)` and `\(\frac{a}{b}\)` reproduce in code. I found no evidence that any producer writes a live body under a deleted control, or what Word shows for one, so "person reads a+bc / x / ab" is unproven.
- **T3 is not a Word shape.** MS-OE376 says "Word ignores this element" for `moveTo` in ctrlPr; I read that page only, not the `moveFrom` one. I found no evidence for T2 either. Neither should drive a fix.

**Severity:** the trigger is narrow, needing an unaccepted tracked deletion of a whole structure in an uploaded document. When it fires for ∑, ∫, () or √, it is a silent wrong formula, which fails the project's own bar. I would keep it as a real defect, scoped to fully deleted structures.

Sources:
- [ECMA-376 del (Deleted Math Control Character), docx4java mirror](https://webapp.docx4java.org/OnlineDemo/ecma376/WordML/del_4.html)
- [MS-OI29500 §17.13.5.13 del](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/0a4ccd31-153b-4a47-b3ff-c070a3743a70)

findings.title: m:phant with show=off or false makes the invisible content real, which can flip a sign
findings.scenario: Doc: a two-row matrix. Row 1 is <m:phant><m:phantPr><m:show m:val="off"/></m:phantPr><m:e>-</m:e></m:phant> then 1, an invisible minus used for alignment. Row 2 is -1. A person reads [1; -1]; output is \(\begin{matrix} -1 \\ -1 \end{matrix}\). m:val="false" gives the same. Only the exact string 0 is treated as hidden; with show=0 the output is correct, \phantom{-}1.
findings.evidence: Ran R5 (control), R6, R7, and H5, H6 (x+ with hidden y gives \(x+y\)). Read: line 258 compares to '0' although propIsOn exists. Read in XSD: CT_OnOff is s:ST_OnOff, a union of xsd:boolean and on/off, so off and false are legal.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The defect reproduces, and a mainstream producer writes exactly this value.

Reproduction on the frozen tree:
- A two-row matrix with show="off" gives \(\begin{matrix} -1 \\ -1 \end{matrix}\). show="false" gives the same. The person reads 1 over -1.
- The show="0" control gives \phantom{-}1, which is correct.
- x+ with a hidden y gives \(x+y\) for both off and false. The show=0 control gives x+\phantom{y}.
- show=1, on, true, a bare <m:show/> and no phantPr all stay visible, which is correct.
- Every wrong result has unconverted=0 and parses in KaTeX, so nothing warns the reader. The character-survival gate passes because the hidden character is still in the source text.
- The cause is line 258, which compares to the literal '0'. propIsOn at line 94 already handles '0', 'off' and 'false', and the runs use it.

Real producer:
- Pandoc writes this through texmath. I read texmath's Writers/OMML.hs from GitHub master. EPhantom is hardcoded to write phantPr with show val "off", at lines 318-320. No other value is written for it.
- Its writer fixture test/writer/omml/phantom.test shows <m:show m:val="off" />.
- The TeX reader maps \phantom to EPhantom, and pandoc's Writers/Docx/OpenXML.hs line 1060 calls convertMath writeOMML.
- So \phantom{-}1 in Markdown or LaTeX converted to docx gives this document. \phantom{-} is a common idiom for aligning signs in matrices (my judgment, not measured).
- The spec's own example for show uses m:val="off" and says "When off, the phant base e is hidden" (ECMA-376 show page on docx4java).

End-to-end run with documents I hand-built in texmath's writer shape, through the real parseSourceArtifact native-docx parser:
- \phantom{-}2 & -3 \\ -4 & \phantom{-}5 becomes \(\begin{matrix} -2 & -3 \\ -4 & -5 \end{matrix}\), so two entries change sign.
- y = x \phantom{+ 0} + 1 becomes \(y=x+0+1\).
- parser_messages was empty in each case.

KaTeX rendering of the two matrix outputs: the show=0 output has one color:transparent span holding the minus. The show=off output has none, so both minus signs are visible. A reader would see the wrong sign.

Scope limits:
- Word itself does not appear to hit this. The Word 14 and 16 samples in the repo spell math on/off as 0 or 1 (seen in settings.xml; none of them contains a phantom). I did not establish what Word 2007 writes.
- I found no real producer of show="false". Only the off spelling is tied to a producer; false is legal under the reviewer's XSD reading, which I did not re-check.
- Reach is therefore pandoc-style pipelines rather than ordinary Word documents, and I have no measure of how often those reach this app.
- The major severity is my judgment and fits a silent sign flip with no warning, but it applies to a narrower population than Word-authored documents.

The repo's second-corpus baseline (docs/audits/2026-11-05-toggle-formula-builder/f3-gold/baseline-second-corpus-F3.txt) already lists 幻影off and 幻影false as WRONG. That sample is hand-built, has no app.xml, and is not independent evidence of real-world use.

findings.title: degHide, subHide and supHide are ignored when the slot holds content, so hidden text is shown
findings.scenario: Doc: <m:rad><m:radPr><m:degHide m:val="1"/></m:radPr><m:deg>3</m:deg><m:e>x</m:e></m:rad>. The flag says the degree is hidden, so a person reads √x; output is \(\sqrt[3]{x}\), a cube root. <m:nary> ∑ with supHide=1 and sup n reads ∑_i x; with subHide=1 and sub i it reads ∑^n x. Both give \(\sum_{i}^{n}{x}\). The existing tests only cover hide flags with empty slots.
findings.evidence: Ran H1, H1b, H2, H3 (round 1); controls R25, R26, C23 are correct. Read: lines 204-215 never read these flags. All three flags are in the XSD. Not confirmed in Word: that it keeps content in a hidden slot. The conversion is still confident against the document's own flag.

verdict.reasoning:
The mechanics reproduce, but the defect as claimed does not hold. The claim is wrong about what a Word reader sees, and I found no real producer of this document. Word itself is the one gap: it is not installed here, so its save behaviour is untested.

WHAT REPRODUCES: the code ignores the flags when the slot is filled. Through parseSourceArtifact:
- degHide with deg=3 gives \(\sqrt[3]{x}\), for val=1, val=on and no val.
- supHide or subHide with both limits filled gives \(\sum_{i}^{n}{x}\).
- Controls are correct: an empty hidden slot gives \(\sqrt{x}\), \(\sum_{i}{x}\) and \(\sum^{n}{x}\), and degHide=0 gives the cube root.

WHAT IS REFUTED: "the flag says hidden, so a person reads √x" is false for Word, by Microsoft's own implementer notes. I did not observe this in Word.
- degHide: "If degHide is on and the degree is not empty, Word displays the contents of the degree in an unexpected place." This is in MS-OE376 7.1.2.27. A search summary shows the same note in MS-OI29500 22.1.2.27, which covers Word 2010 through LTSC 2024; I did not open that page.
- subHide: same wording for the lower limit (MS-OE376 7.1.2.113).
- supHide: Word "will display this argument next to the base argument of the n-ary function" (MS-OE376 7.1.2.115).

So in Word the content is not hidden, and "hidden text is shown" describes Word as well. The claim's reading does hold for the standard's wording and for LibreOffice 26.8, which I rendered: √x and ∑_i x. Readers therefore disagree, and neither √x nor ∛x is established as the one correct reading. Microsoft does not say where the degree or lower limit lands, so the converter's output may still differ from Word's picture. It keeps the character, though, and it does not contradict what a Word reader sees in the way the claim says.

NO REAL PRODUCER FOUND:
- LibreOffice (ran): a natively authored sqrt, nroot and sum with each limit combination writes a hide flag only with an empty slot. Re-saving the hand-made H1, H1b, H2, H3 and H4 strips the hidden content, and the converter then gives the right answer.
- texmath/pandoc writer (read only): hide is on only when the slot is empty; m:deg is empty for ESqrt.
- docx-js (read only, via a published fork, radical code only): degHide is written only when there is no degree.
- The only filled hidden slots in any sample here are the two in F3-新样本.docx. check_second_corpus.mjs:121-122 hand-writes that same shape, and the fixture README says samples are hand-made and no Word was available.
- APIs can build this shape, such as Word's HideDeg and DS.Documents.Word HideDegree. The DS.Documents.Word docs warn it misrenders in Word, so an author checking in Word would see something broken.

LIMIT ON reachable=false: this means none found, not proven impossible. Not tested: Word's own save after hiding a filled slot (UI or VBA), WPS, Google Docs, MathType. Word writing this shape in normal use would flip this field. Microsoft calling the placement "unexpected" suggests it is outside normal use, but that is my inference.

WORTH KNOWING:
1. check_second_corpus.mjs:121-122 and baseline-second-corpus-F3.txt:28-32 mark these same cases WRONG, using gold written on the same premise ("Reads root of x"). Dropping the slot would remove a character a Word reader can see, so those gold entries look wrong for Word. The README reserves gold changes for Main_Designer, so I changed nothing.
2. On a scratch copy, honouring the flags by dropping the slot does not produce that gold. keepsEveryCharacter refuses and the formula is declared: [公式未能转换,见原页;原文字符:3x], unconverted:true. The empty-slot controls are unchanged. If hardening is wanted, declaring hidden-and-filled fits the module's never-guess rule, because readers disagree. That is optional and low severity, not major. I ran this at convertOmml only, not through the notice banner.

verdict.reasoning:
Verdict: the wrong output reproduces, but I found no real producer that writes this document. I refute the claim on reachability, not on mechanics. This means no evidence of a producer, not proof that none exists.

**What reproduces**

- `<m:r><w:rPr><w:del/></w:rPr><m:t>2</m:t></m:r>` between `x=` and `3` gives `\(x=23\)`.
- The same run in a denominator gives `\(\frac{1}{23}\)`.
- All the `w:del` and `w:moveFrom` variants give x=23.
- `<m:r><w:ins/><m:t>` is declared.
The reviewer's runs are accurate.

**Why it is not reachable**
1. Word does put `w:del` inside `m:r`, which the reviewer did not know. MS-OI29500 22.1.2.87(e) says: "Word supports the w:ins and w:del elements inside a math run." But every sample I found has the mark holding the content, not an empty mark beside it:
   - docx4j #348, from an Office 365 document: `<m:r><w:ins ...><w:rPr>...</w:rPr><m:t>A=π</m:t></w:ins></m:r>`
   - docx-cli #27 and #31, whose author reports Word 365: `<m:r><w:del ...><w:rPr>...</w:rPr><m:t>E</m:t></w:del></m:r>`
   - docx-validate #213, from the jubarte redline generator: the same shape, and it cites this as Word's shape.
   The deleted form of that shape comes out right here: W1 `\(x=3\)`, W2 `\(\frac{1}{3}\)`, W7 `\(x=3\)`. It is the reviewer's own T17 control.
2. No source shows an empty mark with `m:t` beside it, or `w:del` inside `m:r/w:rPr`. Note (e) names only ins and del, so `w:moveFrom` in a run has no documented support. The Open XML SDK's m:CT_R schema lists none of the four elements (read in the first 100,000 of about 426,000 characters; its CT_R entry was in that range).

The four repo docx files with math have no app.xml, so nothing identifies a real producer; those I traced are script-built. This check says little, because no real Word file is available locally.

coverage.coverage:
Ran: 4 script rounds, about 125 synthetic .docx documents, all through the real parseSourceArtifact (inlineDocxFormulasOrOriginal, then mammoth) on the frozen tree, cwd server, node --import tsx. Each formula was then parsed with katex.__parse from the client's node_modules, and visible glyphs came from renderToString. The sha256 of all three frozen files still matches the snapshot.

Scripts and outputs, all under <scratch>\verify-f3\wf\hunt : lib.mjs, round1.mjs, round2.mjs, round3.mjs, round4.mjs, round1.out, round2.out, round3.out, round4.out. Generated documents are in the tmp folder there. Case ids in the findings refer to these rounds.

Schema: legality claims were read from the ISO-IEC29500-4_2016 shared-math.xsd and wml.xsd at <app-data-path> . Documents were not validated against it by tool. Only that transitional XSD was checked; ECMA first edition was not.

Not available: Word and LibreOffice were not run, and no browser. So 'a person reads' comes from the OOXML element meanings and my knowledge of Word. Every statement about what Word or pandoc writes or draws is from memory and is flagged in its finding. The legal tracked-change position is m:ctrlPr/w:del. w:rPr/w:del and a direct w:del in m:r are outside the XSD I read.

Ran and found correct (controls, no defect): several m:t in one run, with m:nor and mixed with w:sym; reversed child order (den/num, sup/e, Pr last, rPr after t); m:lit, m:aln, limLoc, grow, shp, vertJc, argPr; type lin, skw and noBar; w:del, w:moveFrom, w:ins and w:moveTo wrappers in formulas; ctrlPr/w:ins; w:sdt in an argument; m:brk at top level and nested; w:del, w:moveFrom and w:del-around-oMathPara at paragraph level; the Symbol map values for F0xx; accent, n-ary and delimiter code points (dumped and read).

Observed, not reported as a formula defect: an oMath in a paragraph-level w:moveTo or w:moveFrom is dropped by mammoth, with its generic unrecognised-element message. Only document.xml is processed; mammoth's raw text omits footnotes by my reading of its source (not run).

Not run: real producer files; the repo's own test suite. Anything checked only by reading the code is marked 'Read' in its finding.

Ran, in-memory database through the real intake, materialize and rebuild chain. Scripts are 01 to 10 under <scratch>\verify-f3\wf\notice-trace\.

Checked and clean:
- The refusal message reaches parser_messages, note metadata and has_parser_messages for inline formulas, oMathPara, body-level formulas, table cells, sdt, ins, hyperlink, smartTag and pict text boxes. Counts were correct there.
- The style filter does not remove the message: an undefined style plus a refused formula keeps it, and an undefined style plus a convertible formula shows no notice.
- Rebuild keeps the notice, an older note gains it, and a stale notice clears when the file now converts. fldSimple, customXml and moveTo lose the placeholder but still get mammoth's own warning, so a notice appears.
- Eight namespace shapes, including strict OOXML, default namespace and a rebound prefix, published correctly.
- UTF-8 BOM and leading whitespace do not trip the parse.
- 44 mutations on two base documents were compared with bare mammoth on the original bytes. No good file now fails, and no file mammoth refuses now passes. The 9 mismatched-tag and lost-closing-tag variants in 09 are the separate finding about a missing </m:t>.
- Prose $ is left alone. A literal backslash in formula text is escaped, so no \) appears inside converted formulas.
- The legacy /api/documents parser (documentParser.ts:328) calls mammoth without inlining, read only. I did not report it because DocumentManager is not mounted anywhere in the client.

Not covered:
- All documents are synthetic; no Word-authored file was used.
- No browser, so KaTeXRenderer's logic was run as a verbatim copy, not mounted.
- No model call, so how often an Agent copies \(...\) into a card is unmeasured.
- Imprint contents were not checked: my query used a wrong table name.
- One rebuild case ('second rebuild') was built with only one paragraph by a harness slip; it still rebuilt twice with the notice intact.

The three frozen files still match the sha256 values in snapshot.txt after all runs. The pre-patch comparison used a scratch copy of the module from git 8f9da86c, obtained with a read-only git show.
